displayReadiness: The current worker only calls prepareScanRenderData when result.positions exists; precise Split instead returns result.scanEdit.positions. With no prepared or stored indexed normals, scanDisplayBuffers selects expanded rendering and the viewport computes smoothDisplayNormals over the expanded mesh. A small shared-Split control demonstrates that preparing render data for the same indexed result instead selects compact indexed display; m2-split-render-readiness-20261028-r1.json. This establishes a code path, not its share of the measured browser peak or native normal equivalence. Moving preparation to the worker or changing normal semantics still requires a separate review and validation.
limitations: This reduces isolated conversion peak but did not make the original GUI/Undo/MCP workflow pass the 4 GiB guard. The remaining large-scan issue is unresolved.
An event-listener microtask sample recorded the same heap before and after the packed message; callback ordering prevents attributing restoration memory from that sample.
The real-browser result does not establish native behavior, public-MCP output equality for the large scan, or full M2 acceptance.
